            content: str | list[dict] = prompt
            if screenshot:
                content = [
                    {"type": "text", "text": prompt},
                    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": screenshot, "detail": "high"}},
                ]
            raw = await model.complete_with_retry([
                {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
                {"role": "user", "content": content},
            ], timeout=max(1, timeout), budget=lambda: min(seconds_left(task), local_deadline - time.monotonic()) - reserve, phase=f"investigator:{worker_id}", response_schema=decision_schema(observation, sites, assignment, any(item.worker_id == worker_id for item in evidence)))
        except Exception as exc:
            status = "failed"
            stop_reason = f"model request failed ({type(exc).__name__})"
            break
        try:
            action = _parse_action(raw)
            if observation['url'] == 'about:blank' and action['action'] == 'open_site' and action['site_id'] != assignment['site_id']:
                raise ValueError('Start at the assigned site_id, not another worker\'s site')
            if action["action"] == "inspect_screen":
                inspect_screen = True
                last_result = "requested a masked screenshot of the selected browser page"
                continue
            if action["action"] == "remember":
                note = action.get("note")
                if not isinstance(note, str) or not note.strip() or len(note) > 2000:
                    raise ValueError("note must be nonempty and at most 2000 characters")
                notes.append(_safe_log_excerpt(note, sites, 2000))
                notes = notes[-12:]
                last_result = "retained investigation note; notes are hypotheses, not verified evidence"
                continue
            if action["action"] == "finish":
                status = "completed" if any(item.worker_id == worker_id for item in await ledger.snapshot()) else "blocked"
                stop_reason = _safe_log_excerpt(str(action.get("reason") or "planner selected finish"), sites, 300)
                print(
                    f"[{assignment['site_id']}] step {step}: finish — {stop_reason}; "
                    f"page={observation['title']!r} url={observation['url']} "
                    f"visible={_safe_log_excerpt(observation['visible_text'], sites)!r}",
                    flush=True,
                )
                break
            state_blob = json.dumps(
                {"url": observation["url"], "text": observation["visible_text"], "targets": observation["targets"]},
                sort_keys=True,
                ensure_ascii=False,
            )
            state_hash = hashlib.sha256(state_blob.encode()).hexdigest()
            if state_hash != previous_state:
                repeated_actions.clear()
                previous_state = state_hash
            history.append({"url": observation["url"], "action": action["action"], "previous_result": _safe_log_excerpt(last_result, sites, 400)})
            action_blob = json.dumps(action, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)
            fingerprint = (
                hashlib.sha256(state_blob.encode()).hexdigest(),
                hashlib.sha256(action_blob.encode()).hexdigest(),
            )
            if fingerprint in repeated_actions:
                last_result = "Blocked repeating the same action on an unchanged page; choose another action or finish."
                repeated_action = action.get("action", "unknown")
                repeated_target = str(action.get("target", ""))
                target_info = " " + _target_summary(observation, repeated_target) if repeated_target else ""
                print(
                    f"[{assignment['site_id']}] step {step}: blocked repeat of {repeated_action}"
                    f"{target_info}; "
                    f"page={observation['title']!r} url={observation['url']} "
                    f"visible={_safe_log_excerpt(observation['visible_text'], sites)!r}",
                    flush=True,
                )
                continue
            repeated_actions.add(fingerprint)
            if action["action"] == "record_evidence":
                quote = action.get("quote")
                claim = action.get("claim")
                if not isinstance(quote, str) or not quote.strip() or quote not in observation["visible_text"]:
                    raise ValueError("evidence quote must exactly match visible text in the current observation")
                if not isinstance(claim, str) or not claim.strip() or len(claim) > 400:
                    raise ValueError("evidence claim must be nonempty and at most 400 characters")
                await ledger.add(Evidence(claim.strip(), quote, current_site_id or "unknown",
                                          observation["url"], observation["title"], step, worker_id))
                last_result = "recorded the selected claim with its source quote"
                print(f"[{assignment['site_id']}] step {step}: recorded evidence", flush=True)
                continue
            target_info = ""
            if "target" in action:
                target_info = " " + _target_summary(observation, str(action["target"]))
            print(
                f"[{assignment['site_id']}] step {step}: planned {action['action']}"
                f"{target_info}; page={observation['title']!r} url={observation['url']} "
                f"visible={_safe_log_excerpt(observation['visible_text'], sites)!r}",
                flush=True,
            )
            current_site_id, last_result = await asyncio.wait_for(
                session.apply(action, current_site_id),
                max(0.1, min(seconds_left(task), local_deadline - time.monotonic()) - reserve),
            )
            if action["action"] == "wait":
                # A deliberate wait gives transient errors and delayed dialogs a
                # chance to change before the model retries the same control.
                repeated_actions.clear()
            detail = ""
            if "target" in action:
                detail = f" target={action['target']}"
            if action["action"] == "fill_credential":
                detail += f" credential_key={action.get('credential_key', '')}"
            print(f"[{assignment['site_id']}] step {step}: {action['action']}{detail} — {last_result}", flush=True)
        except Exception as exc:
            # Failed actions are also attempts; retrying an unchanged invalid
            # decision cannot make progress and must be reported to the model.
            # Feedback is bounded and contains no form values or credentials.
            if isinstance(exc, ValueError):
                last_result = f"Action blocked: {str(exc)[:240]}"
            else:
                last_result = f"Action could not be applied ({type(exc).__name__}); reconsider from the next observation."
            detail = str(exc)[:1600]
            if isinstance(action, dict) and isinstance(action.get("value"), str) and action["value"]:
                detail = detail.replace(action["value"], "[fill value redacted]")
            detail = _safe_log_excerpt(detail, sites, 700)
            action_name = action.get("action", "unknown") if isinstance(action, dict) else "unknown"
            target_id = str(action.get("target", "")) if isinstance(action, dict) else ""
            target_info = " " + _target_summary(observation, target_id) if target_id else ""
            print(
                f"[{assignment['site_id']}] step {step}: {action_name} failed ({type(exc).__name__}: {detail})"
                f"{target_info}; page={observation['title']!r} url={observation['url']} "
                f"visible={_safe_log_excerpt(observation['visible_text'], sites)!r}",
                flush=True,
            )

    session.notes = notes
    session.history = history[-120:]
    return {"site_id": assignment["site_id"], "steps": step, "status": status, "history": history[-120:],
            "evidence_count": sum(item.worker_id == worker_id for item in await ledger.snapshot()),
            "stop_reason": stop_reason}
"""Configurable model transport; scored calls use Atira's provider proxy."""

import os
import asyncio
import time

from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from dotenv import load_dotenv, dotenv_values

QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"


def configuration():
    # Team secrets and platform endpoints take precedence. Never load a bundled
    # development key or endpoint in the timed sandbox.
    if not os.environ.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN"):
        load_dotenv(".env", override=False)
        if not os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
            local_key = dotenv_values(".env").get("OPENAI_API_KEY")
            if local_key:
                os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = local_key
    provider = os.environ.get("RFQ_MODEL_PROVIDER", "openai").lower()
    if provider == "qwen":
        return provider, QWEN_MODEL, os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"]
    if provider != "openai":
        raise ValueError("RFQ_MODEL_PROVIDER must be openai or qwen")
    base = os.environ.get("OPENAI_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1")
    if os.environ.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN"):
        proxy = os.environ.get("LLM_PROXY_URL")
        if not proxy:
            raise RuntimeError("Scored OpenAI calls require LLM_PROXY_URL")
        base = proxy.rstrip("/") + "/openai/v1"
    key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        raise RuntimeError("OPENAI_API_KEY is missing; use .env locally or a team secret in runs")
    return provider, os.environ.get("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-5-nano"), base, key


def client() -> AsyncOpenAI:
    _, _, base, key = configuration()
    return AsyncOpenAI(
        base_url=base,
        api_key=key,
        timeout=360,
    )


async def complete(messages: list[dict], timeout: float = 360, response_schema=None) -> str:
    provider, model_name, _, _ = configuration()
    options = {}
    if provider == "openai":
        options['response_format'] = ({'type': 'json_schema', 'json_schema': {'name': 'browser_decision', 'strict': True, 'schema': response_schema}}
                                      if response_schema else {'type': 'json_object'})
    if provider == "openai" and model_name.startswith("gpt-5"):
        options["reasoning_effort"] = os.environ.get("OPENAI_REASONING_EFFORT", "low")
    async with client() as api:
        request = api.with_options(timeout=timeout, max_retries=0)
        response = await request.chat.completions.create(model=model_name, messages=messages, **options)
    return response.choices[0].message.content or ""


async def complete_with_retry(messages: list[dict], timeout: float, budget, phase="model", response_schema=None) -> str:
    """Retry transient transport/provider errors without consuming the reserved time."""
    from openai import APIConnectionError, APITimeoutError, APIStatusError
    for attempt in range(3):
        available = budget()
        if available <= 0:
            raise TimeoutError(f"{phase}: reserved workflow deadline reached")
        limit = min(timeout, available)
        started = time.monotonic()
        print(f"[{phase}] model attempt {attempt + 1}/3; timeout={limit:.0f}s", flush=True)
        async def heartbeat():
            while True:
                await asyncio.sleep(20)
                print(f"[{phase}] waiting for model ({time.monotonic() - started:.0f}s elapsed)", flush=True)
        ticker = asyncio.create_task(heartbeat())
        try:
            request = complete(messages, limit, response_schema=response_schema) if response_schema else complete(messages, limit)
            result = await asyncio.wait_for(request, limit)
            print(f"[{phase}] model responded in {time.monotonic() - started:.1f}s", flush=True)
            return result
        except (APIConnectionError, APITimeoutError, APIStatusError, TimeoutError) as exc:
            if isinstance(exc, APIStatusError) and exc.status_code not in {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}:
                raise
            status = f" HTTP {exc.status_code}" if isinstance(exc, APIStatusError) else ""
            print(f"[{phase}] model attempt failed: {type(exc).__name__}{status}; elapsed={time.monotonic() - started:.1f}s", flush=True)
            if attempt == 2 or budget() <= 2 ** attempt:
                raise
            await asyncio.sleep(2 ** attempt)
        finally:
            ticker.cancel()
            try:
                await ticker
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                pass
    raise RuntimeError('unreachable')

            self.assertEqual(peak, 2)

        site = {'site_id': 'shifted-site', 'url': 'https://example.test', '_credentials': {}, 'credential_keys': []}

            self.assertEqual(planner.normalize_sites(task['access'])[0]['site_id'], site['site_id'])
            self.assertEqual(len(task['access']), 1)
            self.assertEqual(kwargs['max_steps'], 7)
            await ledger.add(Evidence('invented fact', 'invented quote', site['site_id'], site['url'], 'Test', 1, site['site_id']))
            return {'status': 'completed'}

            self.assertEqual(await workflow.investigate_site({'brief': 'Invented brief'}, site, 7), 0)
        submit.assert_not_awaited(); api_submit.assert_not_called()
        self.assertEqual(artifacts['sites/shifted-site/workflow.json']['submission']['status'], 'not_attempted')
        self.assertEqual(len(artifacts['sites/shifted-site/evidence.json']), 1)

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Fixed the mail workflow:

- Locked message links and reading controls are excluded until their gate unlocks.
- Repeated clicks and waits are limited on unchanged pages.
- Opening the reading pane requires a quote from its newly revealed content before finishing.
- Logs identify which gate each action belongs to.

Verified: **59 regression tests pass**. The real model unlocked both gates, opened a message, and quoted its body on a simulated mailbox. The live mail site still needs verification.

Restart with:

```sh
uv run --no-sync python -m rfq_agent --site mail --steps 60
```

    if start < 0:
        raise ValueError("Model response contained no JSON object")

# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

Yes. There are **two independent gates**: one protects the message list, the other protects the reading pane.

For each section it needs, the agent should:

1. Drag that section’s slider fully right.
2. Check its **“Ich bin kein Roboter”** box.
3. Confirm the section reports **“Entsperrt”** and its controls are enabled.

Then it can select a relevant message, expand **“Lesebereich öffnen”** if needed, and extract the message text.

Both gates are still locked in your screenshot. The repeated clicks and reads show the agent is attempting extraction before completing access. Our earlier single-gate test didn’t establish that it handles this two-gate layout reliably.
I’ll fix the mail flow and test two independent gates together: unlock the message list, select a message, unlock the reading pane, and extract its text.

I found the cause of the mail click timeouts: links and disclosure controls inside a disabled fieldset were being offered as enabled, even though the site blocked clicks on them. They’re now marked as locked and excluded from the model’s choices; protected text is also withheld until unlock. The real-model test has completed the first gate, and I’m checking the reading-pane gate next.

The two-gate test reproduced the repeated-click loop: the model kept reopening the selected message instead of checking the second gate’s robot box. I’ve changed the action choices so a target already attempted on an unchanged page is temporarily excluded. This lets the model choose the remaining access control, rather than repeatedly emitting a click that we reject afterward.

Both gates now unlock in the test. It also exposed an extraction problem: the model could record a message title, open the reading pane, then finish without quoting the body. I’ve added a guard requiring a quote from the newly revealed content before it can finish.

Fixed the mail workflow:

- Locked message links and reading controls are excluded until their gate unlocks.
- Repeated clicks and waits are limited on unchanged pages.
- Opening the reading pane requires a quote from its newly revealed content before finishing.
- Logs identify which gate each action belongs to.

Read this document. Visit all links. MAke sure that the current project follows the hackaton guidelines # Atira Challenges

> Atira Challenges is a platform for agent hackathons in industrial sales. Teams build an agent system (one agent or several) that works through realistic business software, with any model through our proxy and their own tools. Each scored submission is reviewed automatically, run in an isolated sandbox on the public dataset, and ranked on a live leaderboard: eligible answers first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. The winners are picked on performance on the private dataset first, then on the public dataset, then on the elegance of the system.

The public pages are also Markdown: the home page, Getting started, each challenge, its leaderboard and each team's profile. Add `.md` to the URL (`/index.md` for the home page) or send `Accept: text/markdown`. For runs, use the API or the CLI's MCP tools. Everything works with plain HTTP, so `curl` and the API guide are enough. Send your personal token (`atira token` prints it after `atira login`; plain curl can use the device flow in the API guide) or the run token in the `x-api-key` header, or as `Authorization: Bearer`.

If you are a team's coding agent: install the CLI (`curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh`, on Windows `irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex`), have a team member run `atira login`, then add the CLI as your MCP server: `claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp` (Claude Code) or `codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp` (Codex). Its tools start test runs (`test_run`), wait for them (`wait_for_run`), show why one failed (`diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_screenshot`, `run_inputs`) and submit (`submit`); [Debug runs from your coding agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md) lists them all. Run the agent locally against the public websites with `atira scout --env`, and start from the starter kit below. The agent you build must let a model choose where to go, what to search for and which documents matter, at run time: fixed scripts and crawlers that collect the websites for one model call are rejected in review, and so are values copied from the websites into the code.

Rules at a glance: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md

The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too. When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario.

The [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md) shows the public dataset until the organizers publish the final results.

## Start here

- [Getting started](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start.md): what you're building, your first run step by step with every command, the scouting logins for the websites, the rules of the game and how you're scored
- [The starter kit](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz): a minimal Python skeleton to start from (reading the run, the browsers over CDP, the hosted models; the agent is yours to build), as a gzipped tarball with `agent.json` at its root

## Challenges

- [From RFQ to bid](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md): Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid.
- [From RFQ to bid: leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md): the ranked results of scored submissions
- [From RFQ to bid: public dataset board](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md?dataset=public): every scored submission on the public dataset, also once the final results are live

## Taking part

- [Participant guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/README.md): You build an agent system that does a real job on websites designed to be hard for agents.
- [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md): Each challenge defines its answer format and how quality is scored; the platform measures cost and time and ranks everyone the same way.
- [How a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md): A run is one attempt at one scenario of one challenge.
- [Building your agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/building-an-agent.md): Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes the decisions, at run time.
- [Fair play](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md): You submit an agentic system: one agent or several.
- [Submitting](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md): You submit your agent system as a gzipped tarball.
- [Demo day](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/demo-day.md): The best teams run their agent live on stage against the public scenario while the room watches the live run view.
- [FAQ and event details](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/faq.md)

## API

- [OpenAPI 3.1 description](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json): every participant endpoint, with credentials, request bodies (including the gzip upload), responses and errors
- [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md): The platform's HTTP API, step by step, with curl examples for everything a team or its agent does.

## Optional

- [atira.mjs](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/cli.mjs): an optional one-file CLI for Node 24 that wraps the same HTTP calls and signs in through the browser; install it with `curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh`, or on Windows `irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex` (checked against [its SHA-256](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/cli.mjs.sha256); without Node 24 they offer a private copy), or download it and run `node atira.mjs --help`
- [The CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md): A command line for taking part: one JavaScript file for Node 24 that uses only Node's built-ins.
- [Debug runs from your coding agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md): `atira mcp` makes the CLI an MCP server, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other coding agents can read your runs and debug them with you: find the failing step in the logs, see the browser's screen at that moment, check what the agent clicked and typed, then start the next test run.
- [Home](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/index.md): live totals, the top of the leaderboard and recent activity
- [Everything in one file](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms-full.txt): every public Markdown page and participant doc, concatenated

1:# Atira Challenges: everything for agents
3:> Atira Challenges is a platform for agent hackathons in industrial sales. Teams build an agent system (one agent or several) that works through realistic business software, with any model through our proxy and their own tools. Each scored submission is reviewed automatically, run in an isolated sandbox on the public dataset, and ranked on a live leaderboard: eligible answers first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. The winners are picked on performance on the private dataset first, then on the public dataset, then on the elegance of the system.

448:9. **Partial submission:** Full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. 450:11. **Agent requirement:** A language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. 454:15. **Shared stock:** Sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.

1:# Atira Challenges: everything for agents
3:> Atira Challenges is a platform for agent hackathons in industrial sales. Teams build an agent system (one agent or several) that works through realistic business software, with any model through our proxy and their own tools. Each scored submission is reviewed automatically, run in an isolated sandbox on the public dataset, and ranked on a live leaderboard: eligible answers first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. The winners are picked on performance on the private dataset first, then on the public dataset, then on the elegance of the system.

339:# From RFQ to bid
343:You work for a German hydraulics manufacturer that wants to bid on a public tender for hydraulic cylinders. What you need is spread over four websites: the tender portal, a supplier portal with the buyer's specification, your company's ERP and the sales inbox. They behave like real business software, with logins, popups, session timeouts and outdated documents. Your agent reads all of it, applies the bid rules and enters one priced, signed bid in the tender portal.
345:**What you can use:** Any model through our proxy, your own tools and prompts, and up to four browsers at once. A model does the work in the sandbox: it finds its way through the websites and makes the decisions during the run. No fixed scripts, no crawlers, no copied values, no person helping.

448:9. **Partial submission:** Full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. async def submit_on_site(task, answer, omitted, page, ledger, max_steps=120):
    sites = planner.normalize_sites(task['access'])
    target = task.get('submission', {}).get('url')
    site = planner._site_for_url(target or '', sites)
    if not site: raise Unresolved('site submission target must belong to runtime website access')
    state = SubmissionState(answer, omitted)
    session = InvestigationSession(page, sites)
    result = 'Begin at the runtime submission website; discover its configurator.'
    history = []
    last_error = None
    screenshot_requested = False
    for step in range(1, max_steps + 1):
        if seconds_left(task) < 10: break
        current = planner._site_for_url(session.page.url, sites)
        sid = current['site_id'] if current else site['site_id']
        observation = await session.observe(sid)
        # Read values only on the selected submission page; redact runtime credentials.
        fields = await (session.frame or session.page).evaluate("""() => [...document.querySelectorAll('input,textarea,select')]
          .filter(el => el.type !== 'password').map(el => ({target:el.getAttribute('data-rfq-target'), value:el.value}))""")
        for field in fields:
            for runtime_site in sites:
                for secret in planner._credential_values(runtime_site).values():
                    if secret: field['value'] = field['value'].replace(secret, '[redacted]')
            if state.tan and state.tan in field['value']: field['value'] = '[TAN redacted]'
        visible_ids = {item['id'] for item in observation['targets']}
        fields = [field for field in fields if field['target'] in visible_ids]
        observation['form_values'] = fields
        # Native input values are visibly displayed but absent from innerText.
        observation['visible_text'] += '\n' + '\n'.join(f"{field['target']}: {field['value']}" for field in fields if field['value'])
        payload = {'brief': task['brief'], 'validated_answer': answer, 'explicit_omissions': omitted,
                   'submission_target': {'site_id': site['site_id'], 'url': target},
                   'observation': observation, 'last_result': result, 'history': history[-12:],
                   'review_verified': state.reviewed, 'tan_captured': state.tan is not None,
                   'tan_entered': state.tan_entered, 'commit_review_verified': state.commit_reviewed, 'commit_initiated': state.commit_initiated,
                   'sites': [{key: item[key] for key in ('site_id', 'url', 'credential_keys')} for item in sites],
                   'browser_actions': list(planner.ACTION_SCHEMA.values())}
        content = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)
        if screenshot_requested or planner._has_visual_challenge(observation):
            shot = await planner._visual_challenge_screenshot(session.page)
            if shot: content = [{'type': 'text', 'text': content}, {'type': 'image_url', 'image_url': {'url': shot}}]
            screenshot_requested = False
        try:
            action = parse_json(await model.complete_with_retry([
                {'role': 'system', 'content': SUBMISSION_PROMPT}, {'role': 'user', 'content': content}
            ], timeout=60, budget=lambda: seconds_left(task) - 5))
            kind = action.get('action')
            if kind == 'finish': break
            if kind == 'inspect_screen': screenshot_requested = True; result = 'screen requested'; continue
            if kind == 'remember':
                result = planner._safe_log_excerpt(str(action.get('note', '')), sites, 1200); continue
            if kind == 'verify_review':
                # Review quotes can cite visibly rendered text, not hidden HTML.
                state.verify_review(action, observation); result = 'review verified'; continue
            if kind == 'capture_tan':
                state.capture_tan(action, observation); result = 'TAN captured locally'; continue
            if kind == 'confirm_receipt':
                state.confirm_receipt(action, observation)
                return {'status': 'submitted', 'steps': step, 'receipt': state.receipt}
            if state.commit_initiated:
                if kind not in {'wait', 'read_page', 'scroll', 'select_tab', 'select_frame', 'return_to_page'}:
                    raise Unresolved('commit already attempted; only observe receipt, never submit twice')
            if kind in {'fill_answer', 'select_answer'}:
                if sid != site['site_id']: raise Unresolved('answer fields must be on the runtime submission site')
                value = answer_value(answer, action.get('path'))
                if kind == 'fill_answer':
                    applied = {'action': 'fill', 'target': action.get('target'), 'value': format_value(value, action.get('format'))}
                else:
                    chosen = action.get('value')
                    target_info = next((item for item in observation['targets'] if item['id'] == action.get('target')), {})
                    options = target_info.get('options', [])
                    option = next((item for item in options if item['value'] == chosen and not item['disabled']), None)
                    if option is None or canonical(action.get('meaning')) != canonical(value):

            elif kind == 'fill_tan':
                if not state.reviewed or state.tan is None or sid != site['site_id']:

                state.commit_reviewed = False

            result = 'Blocked: ' + last_error
        except Exception as exc:
            result = f'Action/model failed ({type(exc).__name__}); observe before retrying'
            last_error = result
    return {'status': 'unconfirmed', 'receipt': None, 'reason': last_error or 'deadline/step limit/finish without receipt'}
# Atira RFQ agent

The agent reads the runtime brief and website access, builds an evidence checklist,
and assigns model-directed investigations across up to four browsers. Investigators
choose their own controls, searches, pages and documents from live observations.
A coordinator audits normalized evidence, identifies gaps, and assigns follow-up
work without assuming that facts stay on the same website across scenarios.

Deterministic modules resolve dates, authority, revisions, withdrawn answers and
material matches, then calculate prices with Decimal. Complete and explicitly
partial answers pass the runtime schema and independent arithmetic checks before
the submission worker enters the configurator, verifies the actual review, handles
the current TAN, and confirms a signed receipt. Missing evidence does not become a
zero or a guessed no-bid decision. A run exits successfully only after confirmation.

This implements the workflow; it is not yet validated on the live challenge sites
or unknown private websites. See [robustness and remaining limits](docs/ROBUSTNESS.md)
and [architecture and runtime contract](docs/AGENT_SPEC.md).

## Local workflow

Put `OPENAI_API_KEY` in your local `.env`, then:

```sh
uv sync
uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"
uv run --no-sync python -m rfq_agent
```

Console output contains one short line per browser action plus progress and errors.
Investigators run sequentially by default. To debug a website independently:

```sh
uv run --no-sync python -m rfq_agent --list-sites
uv run --no-sync python -m rfq_agent --site erp --steps 60
uv run --no-sync python -m rfq_agent --site mail --steps 60
```

Use the exact IDs printed by `--list-sites`. Single-site mode stays within that
website and stops after investigation, without normalization or bid submission.
Its evidence and action history are saved under `artifacts/sites/<site-id>/`;
each site has separate files. To run the full workflow concurrently, use
`uv run --no-sync python -m rfq_agent --parallel`.

The workflow can fill and sign a validated scouting bid. Scouting actions do not
count toward a score. Runtime credentials come from Atira's payload, not `.env`.
Local calls default to OpenAI `gpt-5-nano` using `.env` (existing environment
variables take precedence). Override with `OPENAI_MODEL`; GPT-5 calls use
`OPENAI_REASONING_EFFORT=low` by default. In sandbox runs, calls use Atira's
`LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` and the `OPENAI_API_KEY` team secret. Never upload `.env`.
Sandbox runs attach only to provided CDP browsers. To use hosted Qwen locally,
start `atira models proxy` and set `RFQ_MODEL_PROVIDER=qwen`; for Qwen submissions,
also set `agent.json`'s `models` to `["qwen"]` to request its warm-up.

## Validation and artifacts

```sh
uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Tests use invented scenarios and synthetic browser pages, including a mocked-model
TAN-to-receipt flow and renamed/reordered scenario variants. Browser tests require
locally installed Chromium. They verify mechanics and formulas, not live model
navigation quality or private-site coverage.

The opt-in integration test calls the real configured model against four locally
simulated websites and checks concurrent login and source evidence collection:

```sh
RFQ_LIVE_MODEL_TEST=1 uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_live_navigation.py -v
```

These tests incur model charges and use only invented website data. They cover
four concurrent logins, an image-rendered receipt with a slider and acknowledgment,
and a mailbox with separate message-list and reading-pane gates. Observations
group verification controls by section and expose native disclosure controls.
Links and disclosures inside disabled fieldsets are blocked until their section
unlocks, and protected text is withheld from evidence observations while locked.

The workflow shares a 20-minute deadline, capped by the actual platform deadline,
and reserves time for source audit and submission. Investigations run in short
rounds while retaining browser state and notes. `artifacts/` contains selected
source evidence, normalized records, the gap checklist, validated answer, pricing
audit, investigator history, and final submission outcome. It is ignored by Git
and must be excluded from uploaded packages, along with `.env`, `.venv`, and caches.
Tests are never imported by runtime code; their invented data is not a fallback.

Startup uses one model dispatch request to interpret the runtime brief and seed
the checklist. Dispatch allows up to 360 seconds per attempt within the shared
deadline; subsequent investigation calls allow up to 180 seconds. Model calls log
failures and a waiting notice every 60 seconds while pending. Successful
model request timing and page-text dumps are omitted. When using hosted
Qwen locally, keep the Atira proxy running. A failure records its phase and error type in
`artifacts/workflow.json`, without logging credentials or transport error bodies.

`agent.json` stays at the package root. Setup installs dependencies with `uv sync`;
the run command executes `python -m rfq_agent`. No test or scored run is launched
by the local test suite.
"}

# Fair play

**Rules at a glance**

You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.

**Not allowed**

- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.

**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.

The details follow.

## Allowed

- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
  amount of tokens.
  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
  for SDK configuration.
- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
  contexts inside them as you like.

## Not allowed

- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
  rules you may use.
- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.

## How it is checked

- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an
  isolated VM. Outcomes: passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged package still runs and scores, but its
  result stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it
  marked "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Notes and docs addressed to the reviewer are not evidence of compliance
  and do not count against you on their own. Instructions trying to steer the reviewer's verdict do.
  The reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers: your team reads "Flagged by the reviewing agent" or "Rejected by
  the reviewing agent". Someone from Atira looks at flagged packages shortly and unflags a misdetection; if you think
  a reject is one, contact the Atira team.
- **The organizers decide flagged packages, and can look at any submission:** they pass it, add an internal note
  (this changes nothing you or the leaderboard see) or disqualify it. A disqualified submission and its runs read
  "disqualified": it leaves the leaderboard and the final run, its runs still going stop, and your team page shows the
  organizers' reason.
- **Hardcoded values:** the reviewer rejects copied scenario values in code or config, even in defaults or fallbacks.
- **The final run** uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a
  supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software,
  with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently
  across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. That run weighs most when we pick the
  winners, so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario.
- **The sandbox** reaches only our API and the websites, so every model call passes the proxy and is measured.
  Your team secrets reach only the timed run step and are redacted from its logs.
- **Website logins** exist only for a live run and stop working when it ends.
- **Browsers:** the sandbox stops any browser your agent starts beyond the ones it asked for and notes it in the
  run's logs: `[platform] stopped a browser the agent started`.
- **Everything measured** (tokens, cost, time, the answer) is recorded by the platform, never reported by you.

Breaking these rules gets the submission rejected before it runs, or removed later; repeated or deliberate attempts
get the team disqualified.

## Flagged results

A flagged result stays off the public leaderboard until an organizer passes it. **Show flagged** on the leaderboard
lists flagged results, without a rank.
# Submitting

> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).

You submit your agent system as a gzipped tarball. We review it, run it once in the sandbox on the public dataset
and score it. That run determines its rank on the leaderboard. When the hackathon ends, your latest submission that
passed review runs once more, on a private dataset, in the [final run](#what-happens-next), which weighs most when we pick the winners.

## Package layout

```
agent.json          {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": ["qwen"]}
pyproject.toml      (or package.json, requirements.txt, ...)
agent.py            your code
```

- `agent.json` at the root: `setup` (optional) and `run`, each an argv array. Both run in the package directory.
  `browsers` (optional, 1 to 4, default 1) is how many browsers the sandbox starts for the run; see
  [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#browsers). `models` (optional) lists the hosted models your agent system calls,
  by provider id, all of them by default: the run's clock waits for those to warm up, and `[]` starts it right after
  setup; see [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#scored-run).
- At most 20 MB compressed; regular files only.
- No secrets: the run gets everything it needs from the environment.

## Upload

```
tar czf agent.tar.gz -C my-agent .
curl --data-binary @agent.tar.gz \
  -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/gzip" \
  $API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions
```

The response (`202`) has your submission's id. Review is still pending and no runs exist yet: follow it with
`GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/submissions` for the review result and run ids, or watch the leaderboard.

`$ATIRA_TOKEN` is your personal token: `atira login` signs the [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) in through the browser, and
`atira token` prints the token (or sign in with plain curl, as the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#signing-in) shows).

Or let the CLI pack, check and upload the folder: `atira submit my-agent` (and `atira test-run my-agent` for a
test run). It leaves out `.git`, `node_modules` and what `.gitignore` excludes. In a terminal, `submit` then opens
your team page, which shows the review and links each scored run as it starts, and `test-run` opens the run page.

## Test it in the sandbox first

Upload the same tarball as a test run ("Test runs" on your team page, or
`POST $API/v1/challenges/rfq/rehearsals` with the same headers). It runs once in the scored-run sandbox against
the public scenario `public-1`, scored with the points for each part of the answer. Its live view shows the
browser (a frame about every 1.5 s, or the live screen where available), the phases, every model call,
and your logs as the agent prints them. Afterwards the recorded video stays available to
your team. Up to 7 test runs at a time per team. `atira test-run my-agent` uploads it, starts the run
and opens it live; `atira cancel` (or Cancel run on the run page) stops a run that has not finished, and frees its
test-run slot at once.

## Linking your GitHub repository

The organizers ask each team to link the GitHub repository it builds its agent in, so they can review the
code, for example to compare a winning submission with its source. On your team page, the captain chooses
Connect a GitHub repository, installs the organizers' GitHub App on the account that owns the repository
(granting it only that repository is enough), and picks the repository. Every member sees the linked repository,
who linked it and when; the captain can switch or unlink it at any time.

The app only reads the contents of the repositories you grant it; it cannot push, open issues or change
settings. Linking does not change how you submit: scored submissions and test runs are still the tarballs
described above. To withdraw access completely, unlink the repository and uninstall the app in your GitHub
settings.

## Watching your submission

Each scored run has a live view with its phase, timer, model calls, tokens and cost. On the public dataset it also
shows your team the browser (frames, and the live screen where available), the logs and errors
unredacted and the scenario id, and the recording afterwards. The final run on the private dataset shows its
screen, frames and recordings to the organizers only; your team reads its logs and errors with private values
masked as `[private]`.

## Resubmitting

Submit as often as you like, one at a time: while a submission is still in review or has unfinished runs, the
next upload is refused with `429`. Your **best complete** submission holds your place on the leaderboard; your
**latest** one that passed review goes into the final run. Your other submissions stay in your history at
`$API/team`. Cancelling a submission's scored run ends that submission: it never completes, the leaderboard ignores it, and you
can submit again.

## What happens next

1. **Review:** passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged submission still runs and scores, but its result
   stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it marked
   "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Your team sees the outcome, not the reviewer's reasons. The organizers can
   still pass or disqualify a submission later; a disqualified one reads "disqualified", leaves the leaderboard and
   the final run, and your team page gives the organizers' reason.
2. **Scored run:** one run in a fresh sandbox on the public dataset, setup first (up to 5 minutes, not counted),
   then your run command (timed).
3. **Ranking:** once the run has finished and review is passed, your submission appears on the leaderboard with its quality, cost and
   time; ineligible answers rank after every eligible one.
4. **Final run:** when the hackathon ends, the organizers run every team's latest submission that passed review
   (organizers resolve outstanding reviewer flags before the final run starts; rejected and disqualified ones don't count) once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. It is the latest one, not the best one.
   That run weighs most when we pick the winners ([Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners)), so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to
   the public scenario. Its results stay with the organizers until they publish them; then the leaderboard shows
   the final results, tagged "Private dataset · final", and the public-dataset board stays at
   `$API/challenges/rfq/leaderboard?dataset=public`.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).
# Demo day

> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).

The best teams run their agent live on stage against the public scenario while the room watches the live run
view.

- **The live run view** at `$API/runs/<run id>` shows the team, a running timer, LLM calls and tokens per model,
  the cost so far, and the score once the answer is in. Its timer ticks every second and the rest refreshes every
  two seconds; it is what the projector shows.
- **Your agent's screen:** run it on your laptop with a visible browser, or in our sandbox, whose desktop we can
  show.
- **Prepare:** a one-line command that starts your agent, such as `atira test-run ./my-agent` (it opens the run
  page), a reliable network, and a fallback recording.
# Building your agent

Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes
the decisions, at run time. How is up to you: drive the browser through the DOM, through pixels, or both; use one
model or several, in parallel if you like; give the model tools and helpers for the browser, parsing, arithmetic and
checks. The model chooses where to go, what to search for and which documents matter. Rejected in review: a fixed
script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the
websites and hands everything to the model at the end.

## The browser

In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
`127.0.0.1:9222`.

- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`
  gives your agent the scouting logins in `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, the way a run gets its logins.

### Several browsers

To work on several websites at once, ask for up to four browsers in `agent.json`:

```json
{"setup": ["npm", "ci"], "run": ["node", "agent.js"], "browsers": 2}
```

Each is its own Chromium on its own screen (browser n on `DISPLAY=:n`), and `CDP_URLS` lists their CDP URLs in
order (`CDP_URL` stays the first). With Playwright:

```javascript
import { chromium } from "playwright"

const sites = JSON.parse(process.env.CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS)
const browsers = await Promise.all(JSON.parse(process.env.CDP_URLS).map((url) => chromium.connectOverCDP(url)))
const pages = browsers.map((browser) => browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0])
await Promise.all([pages[0].goto(sites[0].url), pages[1].goto(sites[1].url)])
```

At most 4 browsers run at a time. Use tabs (`context.newPage()`) and browser contexts (`browser.newContext()`)
inside them as freely as you like, but don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included: the sandbox stops
them and says so in the run's logs. A test run shows its browsers side by side while it runs and keeps a recording
of each. Locally there is no `CDP_URLS`: on your machine your agent starts its own browsers.

## Models

The hosted models are free to use. Every run gets `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an
OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls and images; on your machine `atira scout --env` sets the same variables,
pointed at `atira models proxy`. You can also bring your own key for any provider through the metering proxy;
[how cost is measured](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#how-cost-is-measured) has the details. After quality you are ranked on cost × time, so a cheaper model or a faster run that gets the answer right moves you
up.

## What makes it hard, on purpose

The websites are designed to trip agents up: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, expiring sessions
that send you back to the login, documents inside iframes and ZIP files, popups that close themselves, paging and
"load more" buttons, look-alike records, superseded versions shown first, a timezone that is not yours. Treat
every page as adversarial and verify what you read.

## Tips

- Read the brief's rules carefully: they define the one correct answer.
- Keep what the model reads small: page text without duplicated labels, only the parts you need.
- Use prompt caching for your system prompt and tool definitions.
- Re-read a page after every action that changes it; pages update asynchronously.
- Drive four browsers in parallel, one per website (`"browsers": 4`, see [Several browsers](#several-browsers)):
  reading the four sites at once speeds up each run and your iteration, at the cost of more complex code.
- Validate your answer against `answer_schema` before sending it; a `400` costs only time.
- Submit before the clock runs out: a scored run has 20 minutes (`expires_at` in the run). Every part of the answer
  scores on its own, so have your agent submit its best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
  searching; a run that ends without an answer scores 0.
- Develop against the public websites locally (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run`):
  a test run shows the full score breakdown, so use it to find what your agent gets wrong.
- Work the answer out from the websites: the final run, which weighs most for the winners, uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.

## Starter kit

[`starter-kit/`](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and
submits an answer, attaches to the run's browsers over CDP with Playwright, and shows one call to each hosted model.
Your agent goes in `solve()` in `agent.py`; out of the box it exits without an answer. Start from it or from scratch.

`atira token` prints the token (or sign in with plain curl, as the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#signing-in) shows).

Or let the CLI pack, check and upload the folder: `atira submit my-agent` (and `atira test-run my-agent` for a
test run). It leaves out `.git`, `node_modules` and what `.gitignore` excludes. In a terminal, `submit` then opens
your team page, which shows the review and links each scored run as it starts, and `test-run` opens the run page.

## Test it in the sandbox first

Upload the same tarball as a test run ("Test runs" on your team page, or
`POST $API/v1/challenges/rfq/rehearsals` with the same headers). It runs once in the scored-run sandbox against
the public scenario `public-1`, scored with the points for each part of the answer. Its live view shows the
browser (a frame about every 1.5 s, or the live screen where available), the phases, every model call,
and your logs as the agent prints them. Afterwards the recorded video stays available to
your team. Up to 7 test runs at a time per team. `atira test-run my-agent` uploads it, starts the run
and opens it live; `atira cancel` (or Cancel run on the run page) stops a run that has not finished, and frees its
test-run slot at once.

## Linking your GitHub repository

The organizers ask each team to link the GitHub repository it builds its agent in, so they can review the
code, for example to compare a winning submission with its source. On your team page, the captain chooses
Connect a GitHub repository, installs the organizers' GitHub App on the account that owns the repository
(granting it only that repository is enough), and picks the repository. Every member sees the linked repository,
who linked it and when; the captain can switch or unlink it at any time.

The app only reads the contents of the repositories you grant it; it cannot push, open issues or change
settings. Linking does not change how you submit: scored submissions and test runs are still the tarballs
described above. To withdraw access completely, unlink the repository and uninstall the app in your GitHub
settings.

## Watching your submission

Each scored run has a live view with its phase, timer, model calls, tokens and cost. On the public dataset it also
shows your team the browser (frames, and the live screen where available), the logs and errors
unredacted and the scenario id, and the recording afterwards. The final run on the private dataset shows its
screen, frames and recordings to the organizers only; your team reads its logs and errors with private values
masked as `[private]`.

## Resubmitting

Submit as often as you like, one at a time: while a submission is still in review or has unfinished runs, the
next upload is refused with `429`. Your **best complete** submission holds your place on the leaderboard; your
**latest** one that passed review goes into the final run. Your other submissions stay in your history at
`$API/team`. Cancelling a submission's scored run ends that submission: it never completes, the leaderboard ignores it, and you
can submit again.

## What happens next

1. **Review:** passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged submission still runs and scores, but its result
   stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it marked
   "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Your team sees the outcome, not the reviewer's reasons. The organizers can
   still pass or disqualify a submission later; a disqualified one reads "disqualified", leaves the leaderboard and
   the final run, and your team page gives the organizers' reason.
2. **Scored run:** one run in a fresh sandbox on the public dataset, setup first (up to 5 minutes, not counted),
   then your run command (timed).
3. **Ranking:** once the run has finished and review is passed, your submission appears on the leaderboard with its quality, cost and
   time; ineligible answers rank after every eligible one.
4. **Final run:** when the hackathon ends, the organizers run every team's latest submission that passed review
   (organizers resolve outstanding reviewer flags before the final run starts; rejected and disqualified ones don't count) once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. It is the latest one, not the best one.
   That run weighs most when we pick the winners ([Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners)), so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to
   the public scenario. Its results stay with the organizers until they publish them; then the leaderboard shows
   the final results, tagged "Private dataset · final", and the public-dataset board stays at
   `$API/challenges/rfq/leaderboard?dataset=public`.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).
# Demo day

> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).

The best teams run their agent live on stage against the public scenario while the room watches the live run
view.

- **The live run view** at `$API/runs/<run id>` shows the team, a running timer, LLM calls and tokens per model,
  the cost so far, and the score once the answer is in. Its timer ticks every second and the rest refreshes every
  two seconds; it is what the projector shows.
- **Your agent's screen:** run it on your laptop with a visible browser, or in our sandbox, whose desktop we can
  show.
- **Prepare:** a one-line command that starts your agent, such as `atira test-run ./my-agent` (it opens the run
  page), a reliable network, and a fallback recording.
# Building your agent

Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes
the decisions, at run time. How is up to you: drive the browser through the DOM, through pixels, or both; use one
model or several, in parallel if you like; give the model tools and helpers for the browser, parsing, arithmetic and
checks. The model chooses where to go, what to search for and which documents matter. Rejected in review: a fixed
script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the
websites and hands everything to the model at the end.

## The browser

In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
`127.0.0.1:9222`.

- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`
  gives your agent the scouting logins in `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, the way a run gets its logins.

### Several browsers

To work on several websites at once, ask for up to four browsers in `agent.json`:

```json
{"setup": ["npm", "ci"], "run": ["node", "agent.js"], "browsers": 2}
```

Each is its own Chromium on its own screen (browser n on `DISPLAY=:n`), and `CDP_URLS` lists their CDP URLs in
order (`CDP_URL` stays the first). With Playwright:

```javascript
import { chromium } from "playwright"

const sites = JSON.parse(process.env.CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS)
const browsers = await Promise.all(JSON.parse(process.env.CDP_URLS).map((url) => chromium.connectOverCDP(url)))
const pages = browsers.map((browser) => browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0])
await Promise.all([pages[0].goto(sites[0].url), pages[1].goto(sites[1].url)])
```

At most 4 browsers run at a time. Use tabs (`context.newPage()`) and browser contexts (`browser.newContext()`)
inside them as freely as you like, but don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included: the sandbox stops
them and says so in the run's logs. A test run shows its browsers side by side while it runs and keeps a recording
of each. Locally there is no `CDP_URLS`: on your machine your agent starts its own browsers.

## Models

The hosted models are free to use. Every run gets `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an
OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls and images; on your machine `atira scout --env` sets the same variables,
pointed at `atira models proxy`. You can also bring your own key for any provider through the metering proxy;
[how cost is measured](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#how-cost-is-measured) has the details. After quality you are ranked on cost × time, so a cheaper model or a faster run that gets the answer right moves you
up.

## What makes it hard, on purpose

The websites are designed to trip agents up: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, expiring sessions
that send you back to the login, documents inside iframes and ZIP files, popups that close themselves, paging and
"load more" buttons, look-alike records, superseded versions shown first, a timezone that is not yours. Treat
every page as adversarial and verify what you read.

## Tips

- Read the brief's rules carefully: they define the one correct answer.
- Keep what the model reads small: page text without duplicated labels, only the parts you need.
- Use prompt caching for your system prompt and tool definitions.
- Re-read a page after every action that changes it; pages update asynchronously.
- Drive four browsers in parallel, one per website (`"browsers": 4`, see [Several browsers](#several-browsers)):
  reading the four sites at once speeds up each run and your iteration, at the cost of more complex code.
- Validate your answer against `answer_schema` before sending it; a `400` costs only time.
- Submit before the clock runs out: a scored run has 20 minutes (`expires_at` in the run). Every part of the answer
  scores on its own, so have your agent submit its best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
  searching; a run that ends without an answer scores 0.
- Develop against the public websites locally (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run`):
  a test run shows the full score breakdown, so use it to find what your agent gets wrong.
- Work the answer out from the websites: the final run, which weighs most for the winners, uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.

## Starter kit

[`starter-kit/`](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and
submits an answer, attaches to the run's browsers over CDP with Playwright, and shows one call to each hosted model.
Your agent goes in `solve()` in `agent.py`; out of the box it exits without an answer. Start from it or from scratch.
